claim_summary: Dr-CiK contributes a benchmark resource that turns context-aided numerical forecasting into deep-research tasks with controllable evidence and distractors and evaluates retrieval, filtering, synthesis, and forecast performance.

claim_evidence.quote: • We develop Dr-CiK, a benchmark for evaluating CAF via DR, and release 240 tasks with ground-truth annotations for supporting evidence retrieval and CAF. This design enables stage-wise evaluation of failures from DR to CAF.

evidence.quote: • Level 1: End-to-End. Measures overall forecasting accuracy when a DR agent retrieves context and synthesizes evidence for a downstream forecaster, conflating all three failure sources.
• Level 2: Deep Research. Isolates the DR agent’s retrieval and synthesis quality (Evidence Recall, Document Recall, Distractor Avoidance), independent of the forecaster.

modules.name: Forecast-dependent distractor taxonomy
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK: distractors are generated and rejected according to whether they would change the forecast for the target series and horizon; another task family requires a different target-specific criterion.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - distractor validity is defined by forecast impact
R4:Memory and Context; Planning and Orchestration

evidence.quote: distractors are plausible-looking contexts that can steer the forecast in the wrong direction. To our knowledge, Dr-CiK is the first benchmark where distractors are explicitly forecast-dependent (Figure 2B). Each distractor is generated
a confidently incorrect prediction. Crucially, every distractor remains rejectable: it can be logically ruled out by cross-referencing the task metadata or the observed historical time series.

modules.name: Human-calibrated generation verification
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK: stage-specific judges validate evidence coverage, reasoning chains, and distractor acceptability for the forecasting benchmark; changing the task family changes those acceptance criteria.
rubric_path: R4:Planning and Orchestration; Optimization and Evolution

evidence.quote: Judge calibration. For each generation stage, we design a specialized LLM judge with stage-specific acceptance criteria. These include an Evidence Judge for checking whether supporting-evidence units cover the rewritten context,

each pipeline stage is guarded by its corresponding calibrated LLM judge. We use a generate-until-correct procedure: if an intermediate output fails its judge, that output is regenerated and rechecked until it passes.
